_note: Offline demo snapshot (as of 2026-10-02). Headlines are short paraphrases of public reporting, written for this demo; follow the url for the original source. Live mode replaces this with RSS feeds.

items.title: August CPI rises 0.4%, biggest monthly gain in four months; annual inflation at 3.4%
items.summary: Consumer prices accelerated in August, keeping year-over-year inflation at 3.4% and raising pressure on the Fed to tighten.

items.title: Diesel tops $6 a gallon for the first time as crude holds above $100
items.summary: Geopolitical tensions have pushed crude above $100 per barrel and diesel to record highs, adding to headline inflation.

items.title: Fed raises rates a quarter point to 3.75%-4%, first hike since 2023
items.summary: The FOMC voted 12-0 to lift the federal funds target range by 25 basis points, saying inflation remains elevated.

items.title: Dot plot points to year-end policy rate of 4.1%-4.4%, longer-run neutral held at 3%
items.summary: Officials' projections imply another hike in 2026 with increases extending into 2027; markets price one more 25bp move in December.

items.title: Warsh: 'inflation is too high, and has been for too long'; 16 of 18 officials see at least one more hike
items.summary: Chair Kevin Warsh defended the hike, citing energy-driven price pressure and a labor market resilient enough to absorb tighter policy.

items.title: Credit card and HELOC rates set to climb after Fed hike; savers see better money-market yields
items.summary: Variable-rate borrowing costs typically reprice quickly after a hike while deposit and CD yields improve.

items.title: Dow sheds 4.3% in September and 2.7% for the quarter while Nasdaq gains 1.9% on the month
items.summary: Tech leadership offset weakness in cyclicals and rate-sensitive blue chips as yields rose through the quarter.

items.title: August PCE inflation cooler than feared: headline +0.3%, core +0.2%
items.summary: Both readings came in a tenth below consensus, while personal spending rose 0.9% and personal income only 0.2%.

items.title: Spending outpaces income in August as households draw down savings
items.summary: Personal spending rose 0.9% versus 0.8% expected while income grew just 0.2% versus 0.5% expected.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield briefly hits 5.3%, highest since 2007; 30-year at 5.64%
items.summary: Long-dated yields surged to multi-decade highs before easing; the 2-year slipped to 4.88%, steepening the curve.

items.title: REITs and net-lease landlords down 9%-14% since late August as yields climb
items.summary: Bond-like equities sold off as higher rates raised discount rates and refinancing costs.

items.title: Brent jumps 4.4% to $102 on reports of more U.S. troops headed to the Middle East
items.summary: WTI rose 2.7% to $92.87 as U.S.-Iran tensions escalated and reports said China suspended some exports.

items.title: Energy sector now up 38% year to date, leading the S&P 500
items.summary: Energy, semiconductors and industrials led Wednesday's gains while rate-sensitive groups lagged.

items.title: Gold climbs to $4,203 an ounce as geopolitical hedging continues
items.summary: Bullion added $15.60 as investors sought protection from rising oil prices and Middle East risk.

items.title: Dollar index rises to 102.1 after six straight quarterly gains; euro at 17-month low below $1.13
items.summary: European political uncertainty weighed on the euro while higher U.S. yields drew capital into dollar assets.

items.title: Micron posts strong quarter on DRAM and NAND price gains, signs 26 supply contracts running through 2030
items.summary: Memory pricing power and multi-year agreements with customers underpin the outlook.

items.title: Broadcom agrees to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to lease AI chips
items.summary: Vendor financing deepens as chipmakers help fund the compute build-out of frontier AI labs.

items.title: Nvidia pays final $10 billion installment to OpenAI as round closes at $852 billion valuation
items.summary: The completed investment caps one of the largest private financings in history.

items.title: Anthropic lines up IPO as soon as mid-November, with marketing expected around Nov. 9
items.summary: A listing would test public-market appetite for AI labs amid record infrastructure spending.

items.title: Accenture fiscal Q4 revenue rises 6% to $18.7 billion; full-year revenue $74.2 billion
items.summary: Diluted EPS was $3.29; the company guided to 3%-6% revenue growth for the new fiscal year.

items.title: onsemi amends Synaptics merger to $5.7 billion all-cash deal at $123 a share
items.summary: The revised terms remove the stock component of the semiconductor combination.

items.title: RTX wins $24.4 billion multi-year contract for SM-6 interceptors
items.summary: The award is one of the largest missile-defense contracts as Middle East tensions raise demand.

items.title: Venture Global signs 20-year LNG supply agreement with ConocoPhillips
items.summary: Long-dated LNG contracting accelerates as buyers seek secure supply amid geopolitical risk.

items.title: Palantir partners with Armada to accelerate sovereign AI infrastructure
items.summary: The deal targets edge data-center deployments for governments building domestic AI capacity.

items.title: Fervo Energy's Cape Station geothermal plant enters commercial operation at 33 MW
items.summary: Firm, carbon-free power is in demand as data-center electricity needs grow.

items.title: Synopsys jumps 4.8%, leading the tech sector
items.summary: Chip-design software names rallied alongside semiconductors.

items.title: Mattel surges on reported Authentic Brands interest valuing it above $20 a share
items.summary: Takeover interest lifted the toymaker despite a cautious consumer backdrop.

items.title: Nike fiscal Q1 revenue falls 4% to $11.2 billion, misses estimates; company announces job cuts
items.summary: Revenue of $11.21 billion trailed the $11.33 billion forecast; shares fell about 6% after hours.

items.title: Futures rise as Fed rate-hike expectations fade; 10-year yield eases to 5.24%
items.summary: Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.7% and the VIX slipped below 16 as yields retreated from 24-year highs.

items.title: September payrolls expected at +100,000, down from 162,000, in a 'low hire, low fire' labor market
items.summary: Economists see unemployment holding at 4.1% with wage growth ticking up to 3.2% year over year.

items.title: WTI crude drops nearly 4% to $89 as Brent stabilizes near $102
items.summary: Oil gave back part of its rally while markets weighed escalation risk in the Middle East.

items.title: Gold edges up to $4,217 ahead of jobs data
items.summary: Bullion held near record territory as investors balanced geopolitical risk against higher real yields.

items.title: Nike slides about 6% premarket after revenue miss and layoffs
items.summary: The sportswear maker's results add to signs of a squeezed consumer.

items.title: Next FOMC meeting Oct. 27-28; inflation and jobs data in focus before decision
items.summary: Markets will look to September CPI and payrolls to gauge whether the Fed delivers another hike this year.
